name: Inequality-Adjusted Human Development Index
filter_params: col_prefix=ihdi_; keep only columns where suffix is a 4-digit year (ihdi_2010 … ihdi_2023); melt wide->long; drop rows where value is non-numeric or iso3 cannot be mapped to canonical country name
notes: Columns ihdi_2010 through ihdi_2023 (14 years) in the HDR25 composite time-series CSV. IHDI is only available from 2010 onwards — data pre-2010 are structurally absent. The existing fetcher already handles this prefix pattern (INDICATOR_PREFIX key 'UD-02'='ihdi_'). To wire this enrichment code, add mapping IHDI -> ihdi_ in INDICATOR_PREFIX. Country lookup: iso3 column (ISO alpha-3) mapped via shared iso3_country_map. Scale: 0-1 (higher = better). HDI loss due to inequality is captured separately in the loss_ columns.

name: Gender Inequality Index
filter_params: col_prefix=gii_; keep only columns where suffix is a 4-digit year (gii_1990 … gii_2023); exclude gii_rank_{year} columns; melt wide->long; drop non-numeric values
notes: Columns gii_1990 through gii_2023 (34 years) in the HDR25 composite time-series CSV. Also present: gii_rank_2023 — this must be excluded by the digit-only suffix filter (len==4 and isdigit()). The existing fetcher already handles this prefix pattern (INDICATOR_PREFIX key 'UD-03'='gii_'). To wire this enrichment code, add mapping GII -> gii_ in INDICATOR_PREFIX. Scale: 0 (equal) to 1 (maximum inequality). Three dimensions: reproductive health, empowerment, labour market.

name: Inequality in Income (Atkinson measure)
filter_params: col_prefix=ineq_inc_; keep only columns where suffix is a 4-digit year (ineq_inc_2010 … ineq_inc_2023); melt wide->long; drop non-numeric values
notes: Columns ineq_inc_2010 through ineq_inc_2023 (14 years) confirmed present in HDR25 composite CSV. This is the Atkinson measure of income inequality used to compute the income dimension of IHDI — distinct from Gini. Only available from 2010 (same constraint as IHDI). NOTE: the prefix contains an underscore (ineq_inc_), making the column-selection regex slightly different from single-word prefixes. The existing fetcher's parse_undp_wide handles arbitrary prefixes correctly since it checks c.startswith(col_prefix) and c[len(col_prefix):].isdigit(). Add mapping INEQ_INC -> ineq_inc_ to INDICATOR_PREFIX. Also present in CSV: ineq_le_ (life-expectancy inequality) and ineq_edu_ (education inequality) as companion series.

name: Multidimensional Poverty Index
value_field: MPI value column (exact header varies by edition; typically 'MPI' or 'Multidimensional Poverty Index')
country_field: ISO country code column (exact header TBD — download and inspect Table 6)
filter_params: Load Table 6 (Trends Over Time) from OPHI 2025 XLSX; filter to national-level rows; keep country + survey year + MPI value; one row per country per time point; drop subnational rows
frequency: multi-year sparse (2-6 time points per country, spanning 2001-2023/24; NOT annual for all countries)
notes: CRITICAL CAVEAT: MPI is NOT in the HDR25 composite time-series CSV (confirmed by existing fetcher docstring and direct CSV inspection). Two fetch paths exist: (A) OPHI Table 6 XLSX — trends over time for 88 countries with 2-6 time points each (2001-2023/24); irregular cadence, not true annual series; requires XLSX parsing. (B) UNDP HDR XLSX annex (HDR25_Statistical_Annex_Tables_1-7.xlsx) — cross-sectional snapshot only. Path A is preferred for time-series ML features but produces sparse coverage. The existing fetcher (UD-04) is scaffolded as SKIPPED because the HDR composite CSV lacks mpi_ columns. To activate: implement a separate xlsx-based fetch path for MPI using openpyxl/pandas read_excel, then forward-fill or leave sparse depending on QGI interpolation policy. Confidence is medium because column names in the OPHI XLSX must be validated by downloading and inspecting before coding.
